Synthetic-data iterative retraining 导致 spectral collapse（特征协方差退化），真实数据混入比例存在临界阈值 r_crit ∈ (0.25, 0.3]。详见 paper_framing.md。

- **Multi-seed**: exp_010 (pure seed43) 运行中，Gen 0→1 decompression 与 seed42 高度一致
- **Soundness ~2.5/4**: 达 3/4 需 multi-seed ≥1 组完成 + exp_007 resume 10gen
- **DDL**: May 25 (ARR)

| exp_id | 假设 | GPU | 进度 | 预计完成 |

| exp_010 | pure seed43 三阶段复现 | cuda:1 | Gen 2/10 | ~16-18h |

## 近期任务
- [ ] exp_009 完成 → cuda:0 接力 exp_007 resume (r=0.2, 5→10gen) — Type II 完整 trajectory
- [ ] exp_010 完成 → cuda:1 接力 launch_pure_collapse_seed44.sh
- [ ] 论文修订（批量）：SLV dip magnitude 计算方法统一 + "decelerating" hedge
- [ ] multi-seed ≥2 组完成 → Table 1 改 mean±std
- [ ] Phase E: Discussion/Conclusion/Abstract 最终 pass

## 待修论文问题（批量处理）
1. experiments.tex line 137 SLV dip magnitude 比较方法不一致（Reviewer Loop #7 WARNING）
2. "decelerating" 描述加 hedge → "generally decelerating"
3. exp_009 完整 10gen 数据更新 §4.5 r=0.25 描述

## GPU 预算
2× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 98GB (cuda:0, cuda:1) on rtx6000-diagprobe. ~226h 剩余预算充足。

## 关键决策日志

| D025 | 2026-05-18 | 调整 cuda:0 排期：exp_007 5gen 后先跑 r=0.25 (P0)，再 resume | exp_007, plan_025 |

\subsection{Collapse Phase Diagram}
\label{subsec:phase_diagram_exp}

We now map SLV trajectories across mixing ratios to construct the collapse phase diagram defined in \S\ref{subsec:phase_diagram}.
Three qualitatively distinct trajectory types emerge:

\paragraph{Type~I: Pure Collapse ($r{=}0$).}
SLV exhibits large decompression ($+$98 points at Gen~1, peaking at Gen~2) followed by accelerating contraction (\S\ref{subsec:phase0}).
This trajectory defines the baseline collapse regime.

\paragraph{Type~II: Near-critical Mixing ($r{=}0.2$).}
Twenty percent real data suppresses the SLV decompression phase: SLV rises only 0.8 points from Gen~0 to Gen~1 (vs.\ $+$98 under $r{=}0$), dips at Gen~2 ($2367.5 \to 2358.3$, $-9.2$), then recovers through Gen~3--5 ($2362.5 \to 2379.2 \to 2399.0$, accelerating at $+4.2$, $+16.7$, $+19.7$ per generation), surpassing the Gen~0 baseline by 32.2 points at Gen~5.
Because $\widetilde{S}_2 < \widetilde{S}_1$, the non-decreasing condition is violated and $r{=}0.2$ formally lies below $r_{\text{crit}}$.
The trajectory is consistent with the transitional regime (\S\ref{subsec:phase_diagram}): initial contraction followed by recovery and expansion.
Even at $r{=}0.2$, where SLV dips at Gen~2, the smoothed signal never exceeds the controller threshold ($\max \Delta_t = 0.0019 < \tau = 0.002$), so as little as 20\% real data silences the controller entirely.
The effective rank still rises at Gen~2 ($476.7 \to 481.6$) while SLV already declines, evidence that SLV detects spectral contraction earlier at this mixing ratio.

\paragraph{Type~III: Super-critical Mixing ($r{=}0.5$).}
SLV rises monotonically from Gen~2 onward, reaching 2572 at Gen~10 ($+$8.7\% above baseline), consistent with $r{=}0.5 \geq r_{\text{crit}}$ (\S\ref{subsec:phase1}).

These three types partition the mixing-ratio axis into collapse ($r < r_{\text{crit}}$), transitional, and stable ($r \geq r_{\text{crit}}$) zones.
At $r{=}0.3$, SLV expands monotonically from Gen~2 to 2511.1 at Gen~10 ($+$6.1\% above baseline), with generally decelerating but sustained growth across all eight post-transient generations.
This confirms $r{=}0.3 \geq r_{\text{crit}}$ over the full 10-generation horizon, tightening the bound to $0.25 < r_{\text{crit}} \leq 0.3$.

The Gen~1$\to$Gen~2 SLV change decreases monotonically with $r$, from $-9.2$ at $r{=}0.2$ to $-4.6$ at $r{=}0.25$ to $+5.7$ at $r{=}0.3$, consistent with a continuous crossover rather than a sharp boundary.
The Type~II trajectory clarifies what $r_{\text{crit}}$ marks in practice: not a boundary between collapse and stability in final outcome, but a transition in trajectory shape.
Below $r_{\text{crit}}$, real-data mixing fails to suppress the initial SLV contraction transient but sustains spectral expansion over the observed five generations once the transient passes.

These three types partition the mixing-ratio axis into collapse ($r < r_{\text{crit}}$), transitional, and stable ($r \geq r_{\text{crit}}$) zones.
At $r{=}0.3$, SLV expands monotonically from Gen~2 to 2511.1 at Gen~10 ($+$6.1\% above baseline), with generally decelerating but sustained growth across all eight post-transient generations.
This confirms $r{=}0.3 \geq r_{\text{crit}}$ over the full 10-generation horizon, tightening the bound to $0.25 < r_{\text{crit}} \leq 0.3$.

The Gen~1$\to$Gen~2 SLV change decreases monotonically with $r$, from $-9.2$ at $r{=}0.2$ to $-4.6$ at $r{=}0.25$ to $+5.7$ at $r{=}0.3$, consistent with a continuous crossover rather than a sharp boundary.
The Type~II trajectory clarifies what $r_{\text{crit}}$ marks in practice: not a boundary between collapse and stability in final outcome, but a transition in trajectory shape.
Below $r_{\text{crit}}$, real-data mixing fails to suppress the initial SLV contraction transient but sustains spectral expansion over the observed five generations once the transient passes.

\subsection{Collapse Phase Diagram}
\label{subsec:phase_diagram_exp}

We now map SLV trajectories across mixing ratios to construct the collapse phase diagram defined in \S\ref{subsec:phase_diagram}.
Three qualitatively distinct trajectory types emerge:

\paragraph{Type~I: Pure Collapse ($r{=}0$).}
SLV exhibits large decompression ($+$98 points at Gen~1, peaking at Gen~2) followed by accelerating contraction (\S\ref{subsec:phase0}).
This trajectory defines the baseline collapse regime.

\paragraph{Type~II: Near-critical Mixing ($r{=}0.2$).}
Twenty percent real data suppresses the SLV decompression phase: SLV rises only 0.8 points from Gen~0 to Gen~1 (vs.\ $+$98 under $r{=}0$), dips at Gen~2 ($2367.5 \to 2358.3$, $-9.2$), then recovers through Gen~3--5 ($2362.5 \to 2379.2 \to 2399.0$, accelerating at $+4.2$, $+16.7$, $+19.7$ per generation), surpassing the Gen~0 baseline by 32.2 points at Gen~5.
Because $\widetilde{S}_2 < \widetilde{S}_1$, the non-decreasing condition is violated and $r{=}0.2$ formally lies below $r_{\text{crit}}$.
The trajectory is consistent with the transitional regime (\S\ref{subsec:phase_diagram}): initial contraction followed by recovery and expansion.
Even at $r{=}0.2$, where SLV dips at Gen~2, the smoothed signal never exceeds the controller threshold ($\max \Delta_t = 0.0019 < \tau = 0.002$), so as little as 20\% real data silences the controller entirely.
The effective rank still rises at Gen~2 ($476.7 \to 481.6$) while SLV already declines, evidence that SLV detects spectral contraction earlier at this mixing ratio.

\paragraph{Type~III: Super-critical Mixing ($r{=}0.5$).}
SLV rises monotonically from Gen~2 onward, reaching 2572 at Gen~10 ($+$8.7\% above baseline), consistent with $r{=}0.5 \geq r_{\text{crit}}$ (\S\ref{subsec:phase1}).

These three types partition the mixing-ratio axis into collapse ($r < r_{\text{crit}}$), transitional, and stable ($r \geq r_{\text{crit}}$) zones.
At $r{=}0.3$, SLV expands monotonically from Gen~2 to 2511.1 at Gen~10 ($+$6.1\% above baseline), with sustained positive growth across all eight post-transient generations.
This confirms $r{=}0.3 \geq r_{\text{crit}}$ over the full 10-generation horizon, tightening the bound to $0.25 < r_{\text{crit}} \leq 0.3$.

The Gen~1$\to$Gen~2 SLV change decreases monotonically with $r$, from $-9.2$ at $r{=}0.2$ to $-4.6$ at $r{=}0.25$ to $+6.3$ at $r{=}0.3$, consistent with a continuous crossover rather than a sharp boundary.
The Type~II trajectory clarifies what $r_{\text{crit}}$ marks in practice: not a boundary between collapse and stability in final outcome, but a transition in trajectory shape.
Below $r_{\text{crit}}$, real-data mixing fails to suppress the initial SLV contraction transient but sustains spectral expansion over the observed five generations once the transient passes.

file.content:
We presented a systematic spectral characterization of model collapse across 10 recursive generations of Pythia-410M and identified a three-phase trajectory (decompression, onset, 2.43$\times$ acceleration) confirmed at the 1B scale.
SLV is particularly suited for automated monitoring: it requires only a forward pass, declines monotonically after its peak, and captures volume changes before they manifest as dimensionality reduction.
By varying the mixing ratio across five levels, we construct a collapse phase diagram that localizes $r_{\text{crit}} \in (0.25, 0.3]$: above this threshold SLV expands monotonically (Type~III), while just below it a transitional regime (Type~II) exhibits an initial contraction transient followed by recovery.
A proof-of-concept proportional controller exposes a signal attenuation paradox: as little as 20\% real data silences the controller entirely, and reactive spectral feedback becomes ineffective precisely when prevention succeeds~\cite{scheffer2009ews}.
Preliminary analysis of the smoothed growth rate ($\Delta^2_t$, Eq.~\ref{eq:second_order}) on the $r{=}0.5$ trajectory suggests deceleration in later generations, even under sustained SLV expansion.
Whether this second-order signal provides actionable early warning across mixing ratios near $r_{\text{crit}}$ is an open question.
Even when mixing prevents spectral collapse, monitoring remains valuable: $r_{\text{crit}}$ varies across domains and architectures, and spectral indicators reveal whether the current ratio lies in the transitional or stable zone without waiting for downstream degradation.
Future work should explore cumulative indicators, validate at larger scales and longer horizons, and develop controller architectures robust to their own intervention effects.

\paragraph{Limitations.}
All experiments use a single random seed; multi-seed replication is needed to establish statistical robustness.
We validate at two model scales only (Pythia-410M and a 1B pilot through Gen~3), leaving open whether the three-phase pattern holds at larger scales or with different architectures.
Ten recursive generations may be shorter than production pipelines, and the spectral trajectory beyond this horizon is unknown.

\subsection{Experimental Setup}
\label{subsec:setup}

We use Pythia-410M-deduped \cite{biderman2023pythia} as our base model and fine-tune on a 50K-subset of OpenWebText.
Starting from the pretrained checkpoint (generation~0), each subsequent generation fine-tunes on synthetic text produced by the previous generation, for a total of 10 recursive generations.
At each generation we compute the spectral indicators from \S\ref{subsec:spectral_metrics} on the Gram matrix of 1K held-out last-layer embeddings, paired with three downstream metrics: perplexity, HellaSwag accuracy (0-shot), and distinct-4.

For the mixing comparison (\S\ref{subsec:phase1}), we evaluate three strategies sharing the same total real-data budget:
(1)~\textbf{pure collapse} ($r_t{=}0$),
(2)~\textbf{fixed mix} ($r_t{=}0.50$), and
(3)~\textbf{adaptive} ($k{=}10$, Eq.~\ref{eq:controller}).

\subsection{Spectral Collapse Characterization}
\label{subsec:phase0}

Table~\ref{tab:phase0} reports spectral and downstream metrics across 10 recursive generations, which reveal a three-phase structure.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}rrrrrrc@{}}
\toprule
Gen & $r_{\text{eff}}$ & SLV & PPL & HeSw & D-4 & $\sigma_1$ \\
\midrule
0  & 417.55 & 2366.68 &  9.55 & .413 & .741 & 1942.8 \\
2  & \textbf{496.44} & \textbf{2469.93} & 13.58 & .376 & .515 &  712.0 \\
5  & 479.21 & 2370.17 & 24.59 & .344 & .463 &  741.0 \\
7  & 464.20 & 2304.19 & 38.89 & .319 & .447 &  791.3 \\
10 & 442.46 & 2178.95 & 76.78 & .295 & .426 &  825.7 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Spectral and downstream metrics at selected generations (Pythia-410M; full trajectory described in text). Bold marks the spectral peak before collapse onset.}
\label{tab:phase0}
\end{table}

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/spectral_trajectory.pdf}
\caption{SLV across 10 recursive generations of Pythia-410M under pure-synthetic training (solid) and 50\% real-data mixing (dashed). Three phases are visible in the pure-synthetic trajectory: decompression (Gen~0--2, SLV peaks at 2470), onset (Gen~2--4), and acceleration (Gen~4--10, SLV falls 12\% from peak to 2179). Under 50\% mixing, SLV rises monotonically (except a negligible Gen~1 dip) to 2572 at Gen~10, 8.7\% above baseline and 102 points above the pure-collapse peak.}
\label{fig:spectral_trajectory}
\end{figure}

\paragraph{Phase I: Spectral Decompression (Gen 0--2).}
We identify phase boundaries at inflection points where $r_{\text{eff}}$ and SLV transition from rising to declining.
In the first two generations, $r_{\text{eff}}$ rises from 417.55 to 496.44 (+18.9\%) and SLV increases from 2366.68 to 2469.93 (+4.4\%), while $\sigma_1$ drops sharply from 1942.8 to 712.0 as spectral mass redistributes from the dominant direction to smaller components.
Crucially, this decompression does not indicate improved model quality: HellaSwag drops from 0.413 to 0.376 ($-$8.9\%) and distinct-4 falls from 0.741 to 0.515 ($-$30.5\%) during the same interval.
HellaSwag already declines 5.6\% from Gen~0 to Gen~1, precisely when spectral indicators are still rising; this asymmetry suggests that decompression captures distributional broadening rather than preservation of task-supporting representations.
A monitoring system relying solely on spectral metrics during Phase~I would incorrectly conclude the model remains healthy; joint spectral-downstream tracking~\cite{gu2026sigma} is essential to detect early collapse.
The value of SLV lies not in temporal precedence over downstream metrics, but in requiring no text generation or external benchmark evaluation; it supports continuous monitoring at training time.

\paragraph{Phase II: Collapse Onset (Gen 2--4).}
Both $r_{\text{eff}}$ and SLV reverse after Gen~2 ($r_{\text{eff}}$: 496.44$\to$493.31, SLV: 2470$\to$2441), and this reversal marks the transition from decompression to collapse while perplexity continues its monotonic rise.

\paragraph{Phase III: Accelerating Collapse (Gen 4--10).}
Spectral contraction accelerates: the mean per-generation percentage $r_{\text{eff}}$ decline in Phase~III is 2.43$\times$ the onset-generation rate (Gen~2$\to$3).
By Gen~10, $r_{\text{eff}}$ falls to 442.46 ($-$10.9\% from peak), SLV drops to 2178.95 ($-$7.9\% from baseline), perplexity reaches 76.78 ($+$704\%), and $\sigma_1$ reverses its earlier decline (700.7$\to$825.7), a sign of renewed spectral concentration (Figure~\ref{fig:spectral_trajectory}).

\subsection{Cross-Scale Validation}
\label{subsec:cross_scale}

Repeating the protocol on Pythia-1B (Gen~0--3) confirms the same decompression-onset structure ($r_{\text{eff}}$ peak at Gen~2, SLV peak one generation earlier). SLV's low cost and monotonic post-peak decline make it well-suited as an automated collapse monitor.

\subsection{Adaptive Mixing Comparison}
\label{subsec:phase1}

Under pure synthetic training (\S\ref{subsec:phase0}), SLV peaks at Gen~2 (2470) and declines monotonically thereafter.
With 50\% real-data mixing, SLV rises over nine of ten generations, reaching 2572 at Gen~10 (102 points above the pure-collapse peak); a negligible dip at Gen~1 ($\Delta_1 \approx 0.0003$, well below $\tau$) reflects the initial fine-tuning transient.

The adaptive controller ($k{=}10$) remains silent through all ten generations: $\Delta_t$ is non-positive from Gen~2 onward, and the sole positive value ($\Delta_1 \approx 0.0003$) falls $6\times$ below $\tau{=}0.002$.
Since $\Delta_t \leq 0$ for all $t \geq 2$, the controller stays silent for any finite $k$ and any $\tau > 0$ (\S\ref{subsec:controller}); larger gain values do not escape the paradox.
Since pure collapse ($r{=}0$) produces SLV decline from Gen~3 while fixed mix ($r{=}0.5$) yields sustained growth from Gen~2, and $r{=}0.2$ falls below $r_{\text{crit}}$ (\S\ref{subsec:phase_diagram_exp}), we bound $0.2 < r_{\text{crit}} \leq 0.5$.

Despite sustained spectral expansion, downstream metrics degrade steadily: perplexity increases 58\% ($9.55 \to 15.10$) and distinct-4 falls 68\% ($0.741 \to 0.239$) over ten generations.
This reinforces the asymmetry from \S\ref{subsec:phase0}: spectral health under mixed training does not guarantee model health, and the signal attenuation paradox renders per-generation reactive controllers ineffective precisely when collapse prevention succeeds.

\subsection{Alternative EWS Comparison}
\label{subsec:alt_ews}

To assess whether the spectral patterns in \S\ref{subsec:phase0} reflect a broader embedding-level geometric phenomenon rather than an artifact of a single metric, we compare SLV against six alternative collapse indicators from three signal sources: embedding geometry (RankMe, isotropy), attention weights (stable rank, spectral norm), and output distributions (token entropy, perplexity growth rate).
Token entropy is the Shannon entropy of the argmax logit distribution over a fixed evaluation set and requires no text generation.

Table~\ref{tab:ews_comparison} summarizes the comparison under pure-synthetic training ($r{=}0$).
Two indicators share SLV's decompression-then-collapse trajectory: RankMe~\cite{rankme2023}, the exponential of the normalized singular-value entropy, peaks at Gen~2 and declines monotonically thereafter, though with 2.5$\times$ lower signal-to-noise ratio (4.7\% relative change vs.\ 11.8\% for SLV).
Weight-level and output-level indicators (stable rank, spectral norm, token entropy) change monotonically from Gen~0 with no decompression phase; they cannot distinguish collapse onset from the initial fine-tuning transient.
Isotropy is the least reliable indicator: random sampling without a fixed seed introduces approximately 5\% variance, and it exhibits six monotonicity violations across ten generations, with direction reversals at Gen~4+ that produce a misleading recovery signal.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt}
\begin{tabular}{@{}llcrrc@{}}
\toprule
Indicator & Source & Peak & Mono? & Rel $\Delta$ & Rev.? \\
\midrule
SLV         & emb-Gram  & Gen 2 & \checkmark & 11.8\% & \checkmark \\
RankMe      & emb-SVD   & Gen 2 & \checkmark &  4.7\% & \checkmark \\
Token ent.  & logit     & ---   & \checkmark &  9.6\% & \checkmark \\
Stable rank & attn wt.  & ---   & \checkmark & 14.0\% & \checkmark \\
Spec.\ norm & attn wt.  & ---   & \checkmark &  8.0\% & \checkmark \\
Isotropy    & emb       & ---   & $\times$\,(6) & 75\%   & \checkmark \\
PPL growth  & ppl       & ---   & $\sim$\,(1) &  ---   & \checkmark \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Alternative early warning indicators under pure-synthetic training ($r{=}0$, Pythia-410M, 10 gen). \textbf{Peak}: generation at which the indicator reverses (--- = monotonic from Gen~0). \textbf{Mono?}: post-peak monotonicity (\checkmark\ = yes; number = violations). \textbf{Rel $\Delta$}: total relative change Gen~0--10. \textbf{Rev.?}: direction reversal under $r{=}0.5$ mixing (\checkmark\ = reversed).}
\label{tab:ews_comparison}
\end{table}

The final column of Table~\ref{tab:ews_comparison} reveals that all seven indicators reverse direction under 50\% real-data mixing.
This universality confirms that the signal attenuation paradox (\S\ref{subsec:controller}) is not specific to SLV: any per-generation reactive controller based on these indicators will fall silent when mixing exceeds $r_{\text{crit}}$.
Among embedding-level metrics, SLV offers the highest signal-to-noise ratio (2.5$\times$ that of RankMe) and, together with RankMe, is the only indicator that exhibits a decompression baseline to distinguish collapse onset from training transients.

\subsection{Collapse Phase Diagram}
\label{subsec:phase_diagram_exp}

We now map SLV trajectories across mixing ratios to construct the collapse phase diagram defined in \S\ref{subsec:phase_diagram}.
Three qualitatively distinct trajectory types emerge:

\paragraph{Type~I: Pure Collapse ($r{=}0$).}
SLV exhibits large decompression ($+$98 points at Gen~1, peaking at Gen~2) followed by accelerating contraction (\S\ref{subsec:phase0}).
This trajectory defines the baseline collapse regime.

\paragraph{Type~II: Near-critical Mixing ($r{=}0.2$).}
Twenty percent real data suppresses the SLV decompression phase: SLV rises only 0.8 points from Gen~0 to Gen~1 (vs.\ $+$98 under $r{=}0$), dips at Gen~2 ($2367.5 \to 2358.3$, $-9.2$), then recovers through Gen~3--5 ($2362.5 \to 2379.2 \to 2399.0$, accelerating at $+4.2$, $+16.7$, $+19.7$ per generation), surpassing the Gen~0 baseline by 32.2 points at Gen~5.
Because $\widetilde{S}_2 < \widetilde{S}_1$, the non-decreasing condition is violated and $r{=}0.2$ formally lies below $r_{\text{crit}}$.
The trajectory is consistent with the transitional regime (\S\ref{subsec:phase_diagram}): initial contraction followed by recovery and expansion.
Even at $r{=}0.2$, where SLV dips at Gen~2, the smoothed signal never exceeds the controller threshold ($\max \Delta_t = 0.0019 < \tau = 0.002$), so as little as 20\% real data silences the controller entirely.
The effective rank still rises at Gen~2 ($476.7 \to 481.6$) while SLV already declines, evidence that SLV detects spectral contraction earlier at this mixing ratio.

\paragraph{Type~III: Super-critical Mixing ($r{=}0.5$).}
SLV rises monotonically from Gen~2 onward, reaching 2572 at Gen~10 ($+$8.7\% above baseline), consistent with $r{=}0.5 \geq r_{\text{crit}}$ (\S\ref{subsec:phase1}).

These three types partition the mixing-ratio axis into collapse ($r < r_{\text{crit}}$), transitional, and stable ($r \geq r_{\text{crit}}$) zones.
At $r{=}0.3$, SLV expands monotonically from Gen~2 to 2511.1 at Gen~10 ($+$6.1\% above baseline), with sustained positive growth across all eight post-transient generations.
This confirms $r{=}0.3 \geq r_{\text{crit}}$ over the full 10-generation horizon, tightening the bound to $0.25 < r_{\text{crit}} \leq 0.3$.

The largest single-generation SLV drop in the first two generations shrinks with $r$: $-9.2$ at $r{=}0.2$ (Gen~1$\to$2), $-4.6$ at $r{=}0.25$ (Gen~0$\to$1), and $-0.6$ at $r{=}0.3$ (Gen~0$\to$1), consistent with a continuous crossover rather than a sharp boundary.
The Type~II trajectory clarifies what $r_{\text{crit}}$ marks in practice: not a boundary between collapse and stability in final outcome, but a transition in trajectory shape.
Below $r_{\text{crit}}$, real-data mixing fails to suppress the initial SLV contraction transient but sustains spectral expansion over the observed five generations once the transient passes.

Recursive synthetic training, where each model generation fine-tunes on its predecessor's outputs, causes model collapse: a progressive loss of distributional diversity and downstream capability.
Detecting collapse currently requires costly text generation or benchmark evaluation at every generation.
Spectral analysis of internal representations offers a cheaper alternative, but the spectral dynamics of recursive collapse lack systematic characterization, and no prior work connects spectral indicators to closed-loop prevention.
We track spectral properties of the embedding Gram matrix across 10 recursive generations of Pythia-410M, with pilot validation on Pythia-1B.
Our analysis reveals a reproducible three-phase pattern: spectral decompression (generations 0--2), where effective rank and spectral log-volume (SLV) increase even as downstream performance degrades; collapse onset (generations 2--4), where spectral indicators reverse; and accelerating collapse (generations 4--10), where spectral contraction proceeds at 2.43$\times$ the onset-generation rate.
Among the indicators we examine, SLV is particularly suited for automated monitoring: it requires only a forward pass on held-out data, captures distributed volume changes across all spectral directions, and exhibits post-decompression monotonic decline amenable to threshold-based control.
By varying the real-data mixing ratio across five levels, we construct a collapse phase diagram that localizes the critical mixing ratio $r_{\text{crit}}$ to the interval $(0.25, 0.3]$, separating monotonic spectral expansion from a transitional regime with initial contraction followed by recovery.
We further design a proof-of-concept proportional controller and discover a signal attenuation paradox: moderate real-data mixing prevents the spectral contraction that would activate the controller, so reactive spectral feedback becomes ineffective precisely when prevention succeeds.
